records.canonicalPlayerText: An amphistaff is a serpentine creature genetically engineered by the Yuuzhan Vong to serve as a weapon. It has three weapon forms: quarterstaff, spear, or whip; switching forms is a swift action. In quarterstaff form it has all the qualities of a quarterstaff. In spear form it can be wielded or thrown as a spear; if the target takes damage and the attack roll equals or exceeds its Fortitude Defense, the target moves -1 persistent step on the condition track. In whip form it has reach 2 squares; its tail deals 1d4 piercing damage plus the wielder's Strength modifier and uses the same poison condition-track effect. Instead of dealing whip damage, a proficient wielder can use it to pin or trip as though using the Pin or Trip feat without needing that feat. In any form, the wielder can coax it to spit venom up to 10 squares as a standard action; if the attack hits both Reflex and Fortitude Defense, the target moves -1 persistent step on the condition track. It can spit venom only once every 24 standard hours.
records.summary: Living Yuuzhan Vong weapon with quarterstaff, poisoned spear, reach/Pin/Trip whip, and once-per-day venom-spit forms.

Later darksticks shroud the wielder so adjacent enemies treat the wielder as having total concealment; darkvision ignores this, and the wielder must also be able to see in darkness. A darkstick can be thrown, and if the attack exceeds Reflex Defense by 5 or more it immediately returns to the wielder's hand.
records.summary: Kerestian thrown blade that can return on a strong hit; multiple blades increase damage and some versions cloak the wielder from adjacent foes.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An entrenching tool can be configured as a shovel, pickaxe, or makeshift hammer. When used as a weapon it takes only a -2 penalty on attack rolls instead of the normal -5 improvised-weapon penalty, and the wielder can choose piercing or slashing damage.
records.summary: Multipurpose field tool usable as an improvised weapon at only -2, with piercing or slashing damage.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A fire blade ignores the damage reduction of unattended objects and requires an energy cell to operate.
records.summary: Powered cutting blade that ignores unattended-object DR.

records.canonicalPlayerText: Shockboxing gloves add +1 damage to a successful unarmed attack. As a swift action they can be set to stun, converting the wearer's unarmed damage to stun damage while retaining the +1 bonus. They are two sizes smaller than the wearer and cannot be disarmed or dropped.
records.summary: Worn powered gloves add +1 unarmed damage and can switch to stun as a swift action.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A shock stick always deals stun damage. If its pre-halving stun damage equals or exceeds a susceptible target's current hit points, the target moves -5 steps on the condition track and is knocked unconscious; otherwise resolve the stun attack normally. It requires an energy cell. It can also be mounted as a rifle bayonet; a wielder proficient with that rifle takes no nonproficiency penalty for the mounted shock stick.
records.summary: Stun-only melee weapon that can instantly disable weak targets and can mount as a rifle bayonet.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A static pike is a reach weapon. It can be set to lethal or stun damage, can be thrown like a spear, and requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Reach pike with lethal/stun settings that can also be thrown.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A vibrolance is a large reach weapon whose vibroblade can deal piercing or slashing damage. It is too large and unwieldy to be thrown effectively and requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Large reach vibro polearm dealing piercing or slashing damage.

records.canonicalPlayerText: As a swift action, an ascension gun can switch between heavy-blaster mode and ascension mode. In ascension mode it fires a syntherope grappling dart: a vertical tether can lift the wielder 12 squares per round with roughly 720 kg maximum lift, and a secured tether can form a downhill zipline traveled at 12 squares per round. Ascension-mode range is 30 squares. The blaster mode uses a 50-shot power pack. The weapon carries two lengths of syntherope, which must be replaced after two uses.
records.summary: Heavy blaster/grappling system; swift-switch to a 30-square tether that lifts or creates a zipline.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A sidearm blaster pistol uses energy-trickle technology for 250 shots per power pack. If it is used with Rapid Shot or a feat that has Rapid Shot as a prerequisite, the wielder must spend a swift action to reset its trigger before it can fire again.
records.summary: Efficient 250-shot sidearm whose trigger needs a swift reset after Rapid Shot-style use.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A variable blaster rifle has a 500-shot power pack. As a swift action its power can be changed: the stronger 3d6 setting consumes five times as many shots per attack, and the 3d8 setting consumes ten times as many; the weakest setting uses ammunition normally.
records.summary: Five-hundred-shot rifle whose damage can be increased with a swift action at sharply increased ammunition consumption.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A heavy variable blaster rifle has the same 500-shot variable-power system, with stronger settings consuming ten or twenty times normal ammunition. It also has an ascension mode using a syntherope grappling dart, with the same 12-squares-per-round lifting/zipline use and 30-square ascension range as an ascension gun.
records.summary: Heavy variable-power rifle with high-consumption damage settings plus an integrated ascension tether.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A repeating crossbow automatically recocks and feeds the next quarrel after each shot. Its magazine holds 10 quarrels, costs 30 credits, weighs 1.2 kg, and can be replaced as a move action.
records.summary: Self-recocking crossbow with a 10-quarrel magazine replaced as a move action.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A flame cannon projects a cone 12 squares long and 8 squares wide at the end. Make one attack roll against every target's Reflex Defense; a hit deals full fire damage and a miss half, with Evasion applying normally. Reloading is a full-round action. A tank provides 20 uses; replacement tanks cost 600 credits and weigh 20 kg. On a tripod it is treated as one size smaller for wielding.
records.summary: Large cone flamethrower with full/half area damage, 20-use fuel tank, and full-round reload.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A radiation grenade affects a 2-square burst and resolves its area attack against Fortitude Defense rather than Reflex Defense. Hits take full damage and misses half, with Evasion applying as printed. Targets are also exposed to Moderate radiation for damage and Treat Injury purposes.
records.summary: Two-square grenade that attacks Fortitude and also exposes targets to Moderate radiation.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A smoke grenade fills a 2-square burst with thick smoke that provides concealment and creates a smoke hazard. The cloud lasts 10 rounds.
records.summary: Two-square concealment/smoke-hazard cloud lasting 10 rounds.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The DC-17m Interchangeable Weapon System switches among blaster-rifle, sniper-rifle, and anti-armor grenade-launcher modes as a standard action. Blaster mode functions as a normal blaster rifle. Sniper mode includes a targeting scope, removes the short-range penalty, and imposes -2 against targets at unmodified point-blank range. Anti-armor mode is a single-shot heavy-weapon grenade launcher firing special 3-square-burst ammunition.
records.summary: Clone commando modular rifle switching as a standard action among rifle, scoped sniper, and anti-armor grenade modes.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A mortar launcher cannot attack targets at point-blank range. For line of sight and cover, its point of origin can be treated as 20 squares in the air. Its magazine holds five shells and automatically feeds each shot; shells are statistically identical to grenades.
records.summary: Indirect-fire launcher: no point-blank attacks, elevated LOS/cover origin, and five-shell grenade-equivalent magazine.

records.canonicalPlayerText: If braced before firing, a rotary blaster cannon can autofire into a 2-by-4-square area instead of the normal 2-by-2. If not braced, it takes an additional -5 attack penalty beyond normal autofire penalties. It uses a 20-shot power pack or can be connected to a power generator.
records.summary: Autofire heavy weapon: bracing expands the area to 2x4; unbraced fire suffers an extra -5.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A scatter gun deals its highest damage at point-blank range, less at short range, and no damage at medium or long range. It uses individual shells rather than a power pack and holds 10 shells.
records.summary: Ten-shell scatter weapon effective only at point-blank and short range.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A tactical tractor beam requires a power generator and affects only Huge or smaller targets. A grabbed object can be moved up to 10 squares in any direction and can be hurled at another target within 10 squares using a ranged attack, dealing falling-object damage by size. It normally requires a second crew member to spend a standard action each round regulating power; if not regulated, attacks take -2. On a tripod it is treated as one size smaller for wielding.
records.summary: Huge-or-smaller tractor weapon that moves or hurls grabbed objects; normally crew-served and generator-powered.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A targeting laser deals no damage. Its wielder makes an attack roll that ignores armor bonuses to the target's Reflex Defense. As long as the wielder repeats the attack each round, allies who know the laser frequency gain +2 on attacks against that target with missile launchers, grenade launchers, or vehicle weapons. It requires an energy cell and can be handheld or mounted on a Medium or larger weapon.
records.summary: Paints a target for allied heavy fire: repeated designation grants allies +2 with launchers or vehicle weapons.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A wrist blaster is built into jewelry or a bracer and carries enough power for only one shot. It is intended for close quarters and is masked from weapon sensor scans; detecting it with a sensor scan requires a DC 25 Use Computer check.
records.summary: Single-shot concealed wrist blaster that requires DC 25 Use Computer to detect with weapon sensors.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A darter launches darts using compressed air. Its maximum range is Short. A poison-carrying dart delivers its toxin if the attack successfully deals damage; darts can also carry surveillance taggers.
records.summary: Short-range dart launcher that can deliver poison on damage or fire surveillance taggers.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A snare pistol fires weighted synthcord and can initiate a grab or grapple at up to Short range. A trapped target can escape with a DC 15 Acrobatics check or break free with a DC 20 Strength check. Pin and Trip can be used with it, but not Crush, Throw, or Bone Crusher. Its specialized cartridge holds 2 shots; replacement cartridges cost 25 credits and weigh 1 kg.
records.summary: Two-shot capture pistol that grabs/grapples at Short range and supports Pin/Trip.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The Xerrol Nightstinger uses exotic-gas canisters to fire shots invisible to the eye, allowing a sniper to shoot without visually revealing the firing position. Each gas canister provides 5 shots and costs 1,000 credits.
records.summary: Sniper rifle firing visually invisible shots from five-shot exotic-gas canisters.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A guard shoto has a secondary handle at a right angle. A proficient wielder gains a +2 equipment bonus on Use the Force checks made with Block or Deflect. If its handle is phrik-laced, lightsabers do not ignore the guard shoto's damage reduction. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Defensive lightsaber tonfa granting +2 equipment bonus to Block/Deflect; phrik-laced handles resist lightsaber DR bypass.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An archaic lightfoil is delicately balanced. Its wielder can choose to treat it as a Small weapon whenever beneficial, but it cannot be wielded two-handed. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Delicately balanced one-handed lightfoil that can count as Small when beneficial.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A modern lightfoil is delicately balanced. Its wielder can choose to treat it as a Small weapon whenever beneficial, but it cannot be wielded two-handed. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Modern one-handed lightfoil that can count as Small when beneficial.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A retrosaber is a modern reconstruction of an archaic, corded lightsaber. Its base damage is 2d8. As a swift action, the wielder can increase its base damage to 2d10 until the end of the wielder's next turn. It then burns down to 2d4 base damage for one round, during which it cannot be dialed back up.
records.summary: Corded modernized lightsaber that can overcharge to 2d10, then drops to 2d4 for one recovery round.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An archaic lightsaber uses an external power cell worn on the belt or back and connected to the hilt by a cord. It is weaker than a modern lightsaber and requires a special 600-credit power pack to operate.
records.summary: Ancient corded lightsaber powered by a special 600-credit external pack.

records.canonicalPlayerText: In its default setting a dual-phase lightsaber functions as a normal lightsaber. As a swift action, it can switch to an extended blade that increases reach by 1 square but imposes -2 Reflex Defense against attacks from adjacent targets. A special crystal normally applies to both settings. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Swift-switch lightsaber with an extended mode granting +1 reach but -2 Reflex against adjacent attackers.

records.canonicalPlayerText: When wielded one-handed, a dueling lightsaber grants a +1 equipment bonus on attack rolls for attacks of opportunity. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Curved-hilt dueling saber granting +1 equipment bonus on one-handed attacks of opportunity.

records.canonicalPlayerText: When using Block with a crossguard lightsaber, each successive Use the Force check in the round takes only a cumulative -2 penalty instead of the normal -5. The wielder takes -2 on Use the Force checks made with Deflect. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Crossguard saber improves repeated Block checks to cumulative -2 but imposes -2 on Deflect.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A great lightsaber is an oversized lightsaber. Only Large or larger creatures can use it in conjunction with feats that affect light weapons or lightsabers, such as Weapon Finesse. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Oversized lightsaber; only Large+ wielders can combine it with feats meant for light weapons/lightsabers.

records.canonicalPlayerText: When wielded two-handed, a long-handle lightsaber can forgo doubling the wielder's Strength bonus to damage and instead increase its base damage to 2d10. With Long Haft Form it can be used as a double weapon; the haft end deals 1d6 damage. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Two-handed saber that can trade doubled Strength damage for 2d10 base damage; Long Haft Form enables a 1d6 haft attack.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A lightsaber pike's phrik-alloy haft is not subject to lightsaber DR bypass. The weapon increases reach by 1 square but imposes -2 on Use the Force checks with Block or Deflect. With Long Haft Form it can be used as a double weapon; the non-lightsaber end deals 1d6 damage. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Reach lightsaber pike with phrik haft; +1 reach, -2 Block/Deflect, and Long Haft Form can enable a 1d6 haft end.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A lightwhip has reach 2 squares. On a hit it deals normal damage and can initiate a grab or grapple. A grabbed or grappled target can escape with a DC 15 Acrobatics check. Pin and Trip can be used with it, but not Crush or Throw. A character ending its turn held by the lightwhip takes the weapon's base damage without Strength, heroic-level, or other modifiers. It requires an energy cell.
records.summary: Reach-2 lightsaber whip that can grab/grapple; held targets take unmodified base damage at end of turn.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A san-ni staff is a double weapon. It can be used with Block as though it were a lightsaber. When an attack is made, the wielder can choose to strike with its energy couplings and deal stun damage instead of lethal damage. It requires two energy cells.
records.summary: Double staff that can use Block like a lightsaber and can switch individual attacks to stun damage.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A wan-shen can be broken down into four Small objects; assembling or disassembling it is a full-round action. It increases reach by 1 square and is a double weapon, allowing attacks with both ends using the normal double-weapon full-round rules.
records.summary: Matukai double polearm with +1 reach that packs into four Small pieces as a full-round action.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A discblade is an aerodynamic thrown ring weapon. A trained Zeison Sha warrior can use the Force to return it to hand after it has been thrown; return is not an automatic property of every throw.
records.summary: Zeison Sha thrown blade that trained Force-users can call back after throwing.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An R-9 flash canister has a 3-square burst and detonates on contact. Make one area attack roll against each target's Reflex Defense. Creatures hit take no damage, but all targets have total concealment against each affected creature until the start of the attacker's next turn. Blind creatures are immune.
records.summary: Three-square flash burst that temporarily prevents affected creatures from seeing other targets; no damage.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A datadagger is a decorative code cylinder concealing a needlelike blade. Twisting the hilt extends the blade. Its concealed construction grants a +5 bonus on Stealth checks made to hide the object, and physically touching the wielder does not grant the usual circumstance bonus to notice the hidden weapon.
records.summary: Concealed code-cylinder dagger; +5 to Stealth checks to hide it and unusually difficult to detect by touch.

records.canonicalPlayerText: This antivehicle launcher fires one light concussion missile per attack. Rapid Shot cannot be used with it. Each missile has a 2-square splash radius, and attacks against targets smaller than Huge take a -10 penalty.
records.summary: Single-shot antivehicle launcher with 2-square splash; -10 against targets smaller than Huge and incompatible with Rapid Shot.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A sonic stunner deals stun damage by directing high-frequency sonic energy into a living target. Deaf creatures are still affected because the vibrations penetrate the brain. Only the target hears the weapon's sound, so firing it is otherwise silent.
records.summary: Silent-to-bystanders sonic stun pistol that still affects deaf targets.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A Sith sword is an alchemically treated archaic blade. Lightsabers do not ignore its damage reduction. A proficient wielder can treat it as a lightsaber for Block, Deflect, Redirect Shot, and talents that use those abilities as prerequisites. As a swift action, a proficient wielder can spend a Force Point to add a damage bonus equal to the wielder's Dark Side Score to the next attack made before the end of the encounter; using this ability also increases the wielder's Dark Side Score by 1.
records.summary: Alchemical blade that resists lightsabers, supports Block/Deflect/Redirect Shot, and can spend a Force Point for Dark Side Score bonus damage.
notes: Current repo prose adds an unsupported 19-20 critical threat range.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A subrepeating blaster is an autofire-only pistol with a retractable stock. Unless the stock is extended, it cannot be braced before making an autofire attack. It uses a power pack and must have the pack replaced after 50 shots.
records.summary: Autofire-only compact blaster; extend its stock to brace it, with 50 shots per pack.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A sniper blaster rifle is an accurate weapon designed for prepared long-range fire. If the wielder does not aim at the target immediately before attacking, the attack takes a -5 penalty. A bipod and targeting scope are mounted on the rifle and included in its listed cost. The weapon cannot benefit from the rapid recycler upgrade. Its power pack provides 10 shots.
records.summary: Accurate precision rifle with built-in bipod/scope; attacks take -5 unless preceded by Aim, and its pack holds 10 shots.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The Deck Sweeper fires only on the stun setting and attacks a 6-square cone. Make one attack roll and compare it to the Reflex Defense of every target in the area; a hit deals full stun damage and a miss deals half stun damage. The weapon must be primed with a swift action during the same turn before it is fired. Its power pack provides 5 shots.
records.summary: Prime with a swift action, then fire a 6-square stun cone for full/half stun damage; 5 shots per pack.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An electronet is specialized ammunition fired from a grenade launcher. It targets a 2-by-2-square area; make one attack roll against the Reflex Defense of each target in the area. A hit deals the electronet's stun damage and grabs the target as with a normal net. At the beginning of the attacker's turn, any target still trapped by the electronet takes its listed stun damage again without normal damage modifiers.
records.summary: Grenade-launcher capture net affecting a 2x2 area; hits stun and grab, and trapped targets take repeated stun damage.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A micro grenade launcher fires miniature grenades and is treated as a rifle. Micro grenades use the normal rules for their grenade type but deal two fewer dice of damage on a successful hit. The launcher holds four micro grenades and requires a full-round action to reload. It can be mounted on a rifle in 1 minute with a DC 15 Mechanics check or used as a separate weapon.
records.summary: Four-shot rifle-class launcher for miniature grenades; normal grenade effects but -2 damage dice, with full-round reload.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A neural inhibitor fires a high-velocity dart that injects neurotoxin into a living target. On a hit, the dart makes a 1d20+5 attack against the target's Fortitude Defense. On success the target moves -1 step down the condition track. If that poison attack fails, the next poison attack gains a cumulative +1 bonus until one succeeds. The poison is persistent and attacks again at the beginning of the target's turns until cured with a DC 20 Treat Injury check. If the target falls unconscious, the neurotoxin dissipates.
records.summary: Poison-dart exotic weapon that repeatedly attacks Fortitude and drives the target down the condition track until cured or unconscious.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A pulse rifle fires a 6-square cone as an area attack. Make one attack roll and compare it to the Reflex Defense of every target in the area; a hit deals normal damage and a miss deals half damage. Its power pack provides 5 shots.
records.summary: Five-shot exotic rifle firing a 6-square cone for full damage on a hit and half on a miss.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A snare rifle fires weighted cord at targets within short range and can initiate a grab or grapple at range. If the grab succeeds, the target also takes the rifle's listed stun damage. A grabbed or grappled target can escape with a DC 15 Acrobatics check or break free with a DC 20 Strength check. Pin and Trip can be used with the snare rifle, but Crush and Throw cannot. Its cartridge holds 5 shots; replacement cartridges weigh 2 kg and cost 50 credits.
records.summary: Five-shot capture rifle that grabs/grapples at short range, deals stun on a successful snare, and supports Pin/Trip.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A Squib battering ram requires two characters to operate: one stabilizes the ram while the other triggers it. It is too unwieldy to use against living, moving targets, but deals its normal damage to stationary unattended objects such as walls or doors. It requires four power packs to operate.
records.summary: Two-person powered breaching ram for stationary unattended objects; uses four power packs.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A modern axe is an unpowered chopping tool that also serves as a melee weapon. The weapon can be thrown.
records.summary: Simple legal chopping weapon that can also be thrown.

records.canonicalPlayerText: An energy lance is a force-pike-like mounted weapon incorporating an electromagnetic pulse generator. Although Large, a Medium creature trained in Ride can wield it one-handed while mounted; a Medium creature using it while not mounted takes a -1 attack penalty. The lance can also fire a plasma bolt, functioning as a blaster carbine without a stun setting and using a power pack with the same capacity as a blaster carbine. The lance itself requires two energy cells, and both its melee and ranged attacks work underwater.
records.summary: Mounted energy lance usable one-handed by Ride-trained Medium riders; also fires as a no-stun blaster carbine and works underwater.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A power lance is an energy lance that lacks the plasma-bolt firing capability. It retains the energy lance's mounted-melee design but is cheaper and mass-produced for cavalry and speeder-bike scouts.
records.summary: Cheaper melee-only version of the energy lance, intended for mounted cavalry and speeder-bike scouts.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A gaderffii, or gaffi stick, is a Tusken pole weapon with a blade or spike at one end and a bludgeoning head at the other. It is a double weapon; both ends can be used in a full-round attack, with the normal -10 penalty to each attack before reductions from feats or talents.
records.summary: Tusken double weapon with bludgeoning and cutting ends; both ends can attack in a full-round action.
notes: Current repo prose gives mismatched per-end damage values; the published table lists 2d4/2d4.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A concussion grenade detonates on contact and affects a 2-square burst. Make one area attack roll against the Reflex Defense of every target in the burst; a hit deals full damage and a miss deals half damage. Evasion modifies the result normally.
records.summary: Contact-detonated 2-square burst grenade using standard full/half area-attack rules.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A flechette launcher is a splash weapon with a 1-square splash radius. Because it is single-shot, it cannot be used with Rapid Shot or another feat or talent that expends more than one shot. It uses special four-shot ammunition canisters costing 50 credits.
records.summary: Single-shot 1-square-splash launcher; no Rapid Shot or multi-shot abilities, using four-shot canisters.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A gas grenade detonates on contact and attacks every target in a 4-square blast against Fortitude Defense. A hit moves the target -2 steps on the condition track, or -1 step if the target has Evasion; a miss has no effect. Creatures protected from atmospheric hazards are immune. The gas also provides concealment within the blast area and between creatures inside and outside it until the end of the attacker's next turn.
records.summary: Four-square gas blast attacking Fortitude; moves affected targets down the condition track and creates brief concealment.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The PLX-2M can fire directly or use specialized heat-seeking/gravity-activated targeting modes that penalize the Reflex Defense of the chosen target type. Its missiles detonate in a 3-square burst and use the normal area-attack procedure. The launcher holds six missiles and reloads as a full-round action. A six-missile replacement pack costs 350 credits and weighs 8 kg. A built-in microrepulsorlift means the launcher does not count against encumbrance while carried as the character's active drawn weapon.
records.summary: Six-shot 3-square-burst missile launcher with specialized targeting modes, full-round reload, and a carry-assist microrepulsorlift.

records.canonicalPlayerText: This four-shot launcher normally makes area attacks in a 2-square blast. After firing, the wielder must spend a standard action to reset the launcher. As a swift action it can be switched to single-target mode; in that mode it no longer makes an area attack, deals 6d10x2 damage, and takes a -10 attack penalty against targets smaller than Huge.
records.summary: Four-shot proton-torpedo launcher; standard reset after each shot and optional focused 6d10x2 mode against large targets.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The BlasTech 500 riot gun functions much like a blaster carbine but favors autofire. In single-shot mode it imposes a -1 penalty on ranged attack rolls; in autofire mode it grants a +2 equipment bonus on the attack roll. It uses a power pack with 50 shots.
records.summary: Riot carbine favoring autofire: -1 single-shot, +2 equipment bonus to autofire, 50 shots.
notes: Cross-source mechanical conflict: Clone Wars p.61 states a -2 penalty in single-shot mode and does not state the Rebellion +2 autofire equipment bonus. Do not choose precedence silently.

records.canonicalPlayerText: The SG-4 is a combination weapon that fires ordinary blaster bolts out of water and miniature harpoons underwater. Using blaster mode underwater or firing a harpoon out of water halves the weapon's range. Blaster mode uses a standard 50-shot power pack; harpoon mode must be reloaded between shots as a swift action.
records.summary: Amphibious combination rifle: blaster above water, harpoon underwater, with halved range when modes are used in the wrong environment.

records.canonicalPlayerText: A siang lance is an ancient sporting blaster rifle with an affixed bayonet, normally wielded one-handed. It can make attacks of opportunity: when an attack of opportunity is triggered, the wielder can choose either a ranged shot with the lance or a melee attack with its bayonet. It uses a power pack with 100 shots.
records.summary: One-handed blaster/bayonet weapon that can make attacks of opportunity with either its ranged shot or bayonet.

sourcePolicy: Supplied published PDF tables, table footnotes, weapon-group rules, and weapon descriptions are final authority for Core weapon mechanics.
Core Rulebook_djvu.txt is the fast searchable layer; rendered PDF pages are used to settle table values, footnotes, and layout-dependent ambiguity.

The user-accepted consolidated Weapon Qualities contract is represented structurally (including Accurate, Inaccurate, Arc, Stun Setting, rate of fire, availability, and damage-type relationships), but a Core weapon quality is set true only when Core itself establishes it.
Phase 1 authority supplies identity/prose continuity. Repository values and tags are comparison evidence only and never determine published rules.

baseDamage.authority: diceCount, dieSize, and flatBonus are the structured base authority; formula is derived/display compatibility data
baseDamage.rule: Runtime modifiers may add dice, change die size, or add bonuses without rewriting the persisted canonical base profile. Effective damage is never persisted back into baseDamage.
baseDamage.modifierInherited: modifier = flat bonus to an existing attack (appliesTo); inherited = the profile has no standalone dice and uses the wearer's existing attack (appliesTo/formula "unarmed"), e.g. Combat Gloves, Vibroknucklers, Stunning Gauntlet.
baseDamage.variesByPayload: A launcher profile whose damage comes entirely from the selected payloadProfiles[] entry (Wrist Rocket Launcher); never assign it a fixed formula.

rules: A normal stun setting is an alternate operating mode, not a second unrelated weapon identity.
The schema supports same-as-base stun damage when a source uses that rule.
When the printed table gives an explicit stun value, preserve it as damageMode=explicit even when it happens to equal normal damage.
A ranged weapon actually set to Stun has a maximum range of 6 squares unless a source says otherwise.
Native stun weapons such as a stun grenade are not automatically subject to the 6-square stun-setting cap merely because their damage is stun.
Ammunition-dependent launchers inherit normal/stun behavior from the ammunition they fire.

activation.rule: null when capability is none. A per-attack stun choice (San-Ni Staff: "optional-per-attack", declared at attack time, no action) is distinct from a persistent setting switched by an action. Prior books backfilled: setting -> persistent-setting (action only where the record states stunSwitchAction), native-stun -> native, ammunition-dependent -> ammunition-dependent.

operatingModes.rule: Only one alternate setting beyond the default may be active at a time. Autofire-only weapons that also have a stun setting can retain autofire while using stun, per the accepted Weapon Qualities rule.

damageType.rule: AND/OR semantics are canonical data. Ion remains a qualifier of the printed energy damage rather than being flattened into an unrelated type.
damageType.unspecified: mode "unspecified" with no types: the source gives a damage amount but no damage type (Long-Handle Lightsaber / Lightsaber Pike 1d6 haft end). Never guess a type.

definitions.accurate: No attack penalty at Short range.
definitions.inaccurate: Cannot attack targets at Long range.
definitions.arc: Cannot attack targets at Point-Blank range.
definitions.ignoresDR: Weapon damage ignores Damage Reduction except where a source states an exception.
definitions.areaEffect: Weapon uses an area-attack rule established by source text/table footnote.
definitions.autofireOnly: Weapon operates only in Autofire mode.
definitions.doubleWeapon: Weapon has two usable ends/profiles under the double-weapon rules.
definitions.thrown: Weapon is explicitly throwable as a weapon, not merely improvised-thrown.

qualities.rule: Qualities are source facts. Never infer Accurate, Inaccurate, Arc, DR bypass, or other qualities from names, current repo tags, or convenience assumptions.
qualities.conditionalRule: Context-dependent qualities remain in conditionalQualities and do not overwrite the intrinsic base boolean.
qualities.sourceClaimSemantics: A false quality value means this source claim does not establish the quality. It is not a universal negative across all later publications. During 203-identity reconciliation, a later source may add a quality, narrow it conditionally, or create a source conflict that must be adjudicated.

range.rule: Persist a canonical profile/mode plus quality effects; do not reduce range authority to one arbitrary maximum-range string.

allowedBands.rule: range.allowedBands lists the bands from which an attack may actually be made. It is derived from the printed range profile minus the source-defined consequence of the weapon qualities, and is stored beside (never instead of) the base bands and the quality booleans. qualityEffects.pointBlankAllowed/mediumAllowed/longAllowed must agree with it.

range.fixedMaximum: Utility profiles with a printed fixed reach (Ascension mode: maxSquares 30) use mode "fixed-maximum" with maxSquares; no bands.

penaltyApplication.rule: range.penaltyApplication states what the range-band penalty modifies. Ranged ranges default to "attack"; melee and unestablished ranges are null. CR-1 Blast Cannon applies penalties to damage rolls ("damage").

hardMaxSquares.rule: range.hardMaxSquares is an absolute cap inside the normal bands (Gee-Tech 12 Defender: 3 squares). null on every other range object.

range.ranged without a printed profile: range.mode "ranged" with profileId null (Wrist Rocket Launcher: the source assigns no range profile) must have null bands and allowedBands; never infer a profile from the repo.

damageReductionInteraction.rule: qualities.ignoresDR is the required yes/no shorthand. damageReductionInteraction carries the detailed rule and must agree with it. Penetrating Attack and other actor mechanics remain runtime modifiers rather than mutating the weapon base field.

weaponSizeAndHandedness.rule: Persist printed weapon size. Light/one-handed/two-handed is normally derived from weapon size relative to wielder size.
weaponSizeAndHandedness.guardrail: Do not stamp static isLight/isTwoHanded from weapon names. Explicit source requirements such as a mounted bayonet requiring two hands remain contextual operation rules.

availability.rule: Rare is independent from legal restriction, allowing combinations such as Licensed + Rare.
availability.unpublishedRestriction: restriction may be null only when the source publishes no table entry for the weapon (Retrosaber); cost/size/weight are then null too and must not be taken from the repo.

rateOfFire.rule: Use [S], [A], or [S,A] for ranged weapons. autofireOnly is a separate quality established by source text. "Special" is used only when the printed table says Special (KOTOR Sonic Disruptor); it requires operation.specialRateOfFire and is never coerced to S or A.

resourceAndAmmunition.rule: Preserve power source/ammunition kind, capacity, reload action, replacement units, and alternate source. Null capacity means unstated or effectively indefinite, never zero by default.

branchFamilyMapping.rule: system.weaponCategory remains the base branch mirror melee/ranged. system.subcategory is the canonical family field. system.proficiency is a compatibility/proficiency key and must agree with source group.
branchFamilyMapping.exoticRule: Exotic proficiency remains identity-specific even if a compatibility field uses the token exotic.

compatibilityFields.rule: These are implementation compatibility surfaces, not independent canonical authorities. Claude should extend verification around them but must not mutate production records during Phase 2 certification.

schemaContract.authorityInvariant: Published fact -> structured canonical field -> explicit schema mapping -> later production mutation. Repo data never flows backward into canonical authority.

attackProfiles.rule: Each profile is one mechanically distinct way to use the weapon. Ordinary weapons have one profile "primary"; double weapons "end1"/"end2"; source-published alternates (modes, configurations, thrown vs melee) get their own ids. Profile fields override record-level fields for that profile. Never invent alternate profiles.

attackResolution.note: "unspecified" = the certified authority does not capture the miss rule (Core/KOTOR area weapons).
attackResolution.onMissNote: effect-still-applies-to-all-targets: an area effect with no damage (R-9 Flash Canister concealment) applies to every creature in the burst whether or not the attack hits.

area.rule: enabled=false for non-area profiles. Geometry is only filled from certified source facts.

attackProfiles.resourceConsumption: attackProfiles[].resourceConsumption is null or {resource, baseUnits, multiplier} plus source-specific extras (stunUnits, autofireUnits, reason).

qualityParameters.rule: Source-specific parameters of a named quality. Core/KOTOR Inaccurate = cannot attack at Long range (allowedBands pointBlank, short, medium). Galaxy at War Inaccurate = cannot attack at Medium or Long range (allowedBands pointBlank, short). Never flatten one book definition into another; an Inaccurate record must state its allowedBands here.
qualityParameters.inaccurateShapes: qualityParameters.inaccurate.allowedBands is canonical; a source-stated longAllowed:false is equivalent to allowedBands pointBlank/short/medium.

modeProfiles.rule: Switchable weapon modes map to attack profiles. [] when the source publishes no mode-specific mechanics. switchAction may be null when the source does not state one.

resourceConsumption.rule: null when no special consumption rule exists; multipliers (e.g. 1x/5x/10x shots) live on the mode/profile.

conditionalDamage.rule: Record-level array; [] unless a certified source rule changes damage by condition (e.g. Scatter Gun by range band, Darkstick held two in one hand). Entries are replacement profiles (default operation "replace", requires damage) or adjustments: "add-dice" (diceCountDelta, dieSize) and "area-toggle" (CR-1 adjacent +1d8, nonadjacent splash).

preparedAttack.rule: null unless a source publishes a primed/prepared attack (Bryar pistol/rifle). Never create prepared states without source authority.
preparedAttack.temporaryOverrides: Optional preparedAttack.temporaryOverrides (e.g. effectiveWeaponSize) and unpreparedRestriction change effective size or firing eligibility temporarily without mutating canonical size (Heavy Blaster Cannon: Huge, braced as Large by two swift actions).

damageComponents.rule: Simultaneous independently rolled components (Neuronic Whip: 2d8 stun plus separate 1d4 slashing). One damage amount with several types stays damageType.mode "and" and is never split into components.

firingConstraints.rule: null unless a source constrains firing. Generalizes KOTOR specialRateOfFire; a rateOfFire ["Special"] profile must carry firingConstraints and the published Special table value is kept.

defensiveInteractions.rule: Mechanics of the weapon object as a defender or defensive implement, separate from outgoing damageReductionInteraction ("lightsaber-does-not-ignore-own-dr" for Guard Shoto, Lightsaber Pike, Electrostaff, Shockstaff). [] unless source-certified. v2.5 entries carry id + effect (e.g. incoming-lightsaber-does-not-ignore-weapon-dr, equipment-bonus, replace-cumulative-penalty, check-penalty, eligible-for-Block-as-lightsaber); optional condition/value/target. Prior books' type entries gained id/effect.

inaccurateByBook.Galaxy at War: cannot attack at Medium or Long range

conditionalModifiers.rule: Source-defined attack/damage modifiers tied to a mode or circumstance (Riot Gun -2 in single-shot mode; ICWS sniper -2 at unmodified point-blank; Power Hammer -2 with Double/Triple Attack or Rapid Strike; Arg'garok -5 below Strength 15). Modes may also carry conditionalModifiers. Target vocabulary (v2.5): attackRoll, damageRoll, reflexDefense, fortitudeDefense, willDefense, and dotted useTheForceCheck.<Ability>[.cumulativePenaltyPerAdditionalCheck] for Block/Deflect checks. Prior books' "attack"/"damage" were renamed attackRoll/damageRoll. Extra keys (bonusType, replacesDefault) are allowed.

proficiencyRules.rule: Record-level conditional/alternate/simultaneous proficiency or classification behavior (Vibroknucklers while worn; species-specific treat-as rules). [] by default.

objectDurability.rule: The weapon object as a target; distinct from wielder defenses, outgoing DR bypass and defensiveInteractions. null unless source-certified.

integratedAccessories.rule: Accessories the source says are part of the weapon (DLT-20A scope). [] by default; never add commonly mounted accessories.

resourceLifecycle.rule: Booleans only when source-established, otherwise null; required keys on every resource whose kind is not "none". Capacities and reload actions are never changed by these keys.

payloadProfiles.rule: Launcher ammunition whose selection supplies its own damage/type/cost/effects (Wrist Rocket Launcher: 7 payloads). Payloads are subordinate to the parent weapon identity, never separate weapons. [] by default; Core Grenade Launcher and Galaxy at War Mortar Launcher may later reference a grenade payload family once that family is certified. Each payload carries damage (full payload profile) or effect (Concealed Dart Launcher sedative / contact-poison darts).

wieldingRules.rule: Source-defined handedness, effective-size choices, ability-bonus substitutions and wielder-size-dependent eligibility. A wielder-size gate on feats/talents (Great Lightsaber) is NOT a prohibition on smaller wielders. [] by default. Entries may also be pure condition rules with source-specific keys (Heavy Blaster Cannon: unbraced size restriction, braced effective size).

stateMachine.rule: Forced timed transitions (Retrosaber: normal -> overcharge -> burnout -> normal, locked out of overcharge during burnout). Selectable modes stay modeProfiles. null by default.

activationRequirements.rule: Gates a profile/mode behind an action, feat (Long Haft Form), wielding state or choice; the profile is never always-available. [] by default.

triggeredEffects.rule: Delayed/repeated damage or control effects. canonicalStats.triggeredEffects must equal the profile-level effects in order. modifierPolicy states which modifiers apply to the damage (Lightwhip: base weapon damage only, excluding Strength, half heroic level and all other modifiers). null when not stated.

constructionRules.rule: Weapon-specific construction DCs, crystal inheritance, mutually exclusive configurations (Retrosaber DC 25; dual-phase crystals). null by default.

configurationStates.rule: Noncombat physical states with transition action and usability (Wan-Shen disassembly, archaic power cord, Snap Baton, Czerka Adventurer). attackUsable null = not stated. [] by default.

criticalEffects.rule: Source-defined critical-hit transformations of base dice (Hunting Blaster Carbine d8 -> d10; Heavy Assault Blaster Rifle d10 -> d12, dice count preserved) without altering persistent base damage. [] by default; never inferred from repo traits.

conditionalQualities.rule: A published base quality enabled or disabled under a source condition (Sporting Blaster Carbine: table-Inaccurate, not Inaccurate while wielded two-handed). The base qualities boolean is never erased. Prior entries converted: value -> state, condition -> when.description, scope "weapon", effect null.

technologyClassification.rule: Source-defined technology categories (biotech: Treat Injury instead of Mechanics, Knowledge (life sciences) instead of Knowledge (technology), harder to sense and grasp with the Force, Biotech Specialist instead of Tech Specialist). {tags:[],rules:[]} by default.

deliveryMethod.rule: Separates physical delivery from the rules range classification (Razor Bug / Thud Bug thrown by hand but use simple-weapon ranges). null by default; qualities.thrown is not set merely because an object is hurled when the source assigns another range classification.
